checks: That the customweightmultiplier() variable is >= 0 on every observation the estimation sample will actually use (`cap assert `customweightmultiplier' >= 0 if `ifstatement''). Missing values are exempt because they were already marked out of `ifvar' by the non-missing loop 14 lines above; the check is folded onto `ifstatement' so negative values confined to rows the sample discards anyway are tolerated (the G15A precedent). Errors 411 when violated.
without_it: The run completes with rc 0 and no message, and returns numbers that look entirely ordinary but are wrong. cwm is deliberately NOT folded into `w' (the regression weight) — the comment at L621-634 says so explicitly — so the regression is untouched and the fit looks normal. cwm enters only the estimand weights built at L1630-1650 (`customweighttext' = `* `customweightmultiplier''), which become w_att / w_att_it / w_att_i / w_att_itime and are handed to margins as [iw=] or [aw=] at L2030, L2089, L2153 etc. Stata's iweight plumbing (the default when the user supplies no weights: L640-ish sets `local weight iw') accepts negative weights without complaint, so the reported effects are weighted averages taken with signed weights: individual cells enter with the wrong sign, the weight mass can shrink toward zero and inflate the ratio, and the escomp shares (built from the same w_att at L3832) come out wrong too. The author probed exactly this and recorded rc 0. There is a MIXED tail: if the negative weights are large enough that a cell's weight mass cancels to near zero, the ratio blows up into an absurd magnitude a user would notice (case 2), and wooldid_fcol's comment documents a cell whose signed weights cancel to exactly zero. But the typical input — a variable that is meant to be a population weight and has a handful of negative entries from a coding error — lands squarely in case 3. The display never warns; it prints only "Note: all Estimates Shown Apply <var> Weights Post-Estimation" (L11369) whatever the sign.
evidence: Comment L711-714: "NFCOMP-02: the customweightmultiplier() domain is documented as >= 0 but was never enforced - a negative value silently corrupts weight masses, estimates, and the escomp shares under the default iweight plumbing (probed rc 0, no message)." Corroborated by wooldid_solved_issues.md:410 "negative values silently corrupted weights and estimates (rc 0)" and test/suite/PREREG_2026-08-23.md:29 "NFCOMP-02 customweightmultiplier >= 0 screen (rc0 -> error)." The same weight family's sensitivity is measured in wooldid_fcol at L5636-5638: a customweightmultiplier() of exactly 0 moved "a pre-trend horizon moving p .167 -> .0022", and L5643-5644 calls signed cwm under safety(off) "caveat emptor".

checks: F13 onset-constancy: that the (anticipation-shifted, window-screened) treatment onset variable `ttre' takes exactly one value within each `i', over the screened estimation sample. Implemented as two `gegen by(i)' passes over cond(ttre >= ., -8.99e+307, ttre) — folding every missing flavor to one sentinel so an all-missing (never-treated) unit passes while a unit mixing missing and non-missing onsets fails — then `assert f13ttremin == f13ttremax'. Errors 459 and names the smallest offending `i'. Skipped inside a replication (`wdrepmode' == 1).
without_it: The run completes and returns plausible event-study and ATT numbers that are wrong, with nothing to alert the user. The _i/_t construction downstream reads `ttre' row by row (`gen _t = t - ttre' at L816, and the same in wooldid_reltime L12080), so a unit whose onset is recorded only from the onset period forward — an extremely common data shape — has its pre-treatment rows carry a missing onset, which makes those rows look never-treated: they join the pooled control group (_i = 0, _t = 0 via L928-929) and the unit is used as its own control. The estimate stays in a normal range and simply attenuates. The other two documented causes are equally quiet: two genuinely different underlying units merged under one `i' value get split across two cohorts and the event-study horizons shift; and IDs stored as float round distinct large IDs together, silently merging units whose onsets differ. wooldid_reltime's own comment (L12053-12057) confirms the downstream consequence when a within-unit-varying ttre does reach it: "a silent collinearity route (dropped treated dummies, biased estimates)". No downstream screen catches this — the regression is well-posed, the cells are populated, and the header shows nothing unusual.
evidence: Comment L754-758: "the _i/_t construction below assumes cohort-level timing - exactly one treatment onset per unit. rows of the same i carrying different onsets, or a mix of missing and non-missing onsets, are silently re-timed row by row: part of the unit joins the control pool or a second cohort, shifting event-study horizons and pre-trends with no error." The error message at L783 repeats it: "rows of the same `i' carrying different onsets, or a mix of missing and non-missing onsets, are silently split across cohorts, and part of the group can be used as its own control." review_process/guard_cost_2026-09-16.md independently screened this guard out of its removal candidates for exactly this reason: "F13's failure is silent, not loud. Its own comment says rows of the same `i` with different onsets 'are silently re-timed row by row ... with no error.' A check against a silent wrong answer is never redundant with a later fail-safe."

checks: Nothing that changes the computation. Under esfixedbaseperiod, the two lines ABOVE the guard (L833-835) unconditionally drop every calendar period `t' that contains no in-sample untreated row (`replace ifvar = 0 if controlcheck2 == 0'). The safety block only re-tests the same indicator (`cap assert controlcheck2 != 0') and, if it fired, prints a `dis as text' caution — plus, under contreat(), a pointer to contreatwithin. It does not stop the run and does not alter a single number. Its twin in wooldid_reltime (L12148-12156) is identical.
without_it: Identical numbers are produced, silently, on a sample narrower than the one the user asked for. The typical trigger is ordinary: in a staggered design where every unit is eventually treated, the final calendar period(s) have no control unit and are deleted; the reported ATT and event-study coefficients then cover a shorter window than the data and the options imply, and are perfectly plausible. The only residual signal is the header line "N = ... (`droppedobs' obs dropped from initial sample)" at L11326/11329, which is printed on every run and never says why — so this is a partial mitigation, not a warning. Note that the estimates themselves are internally valid for the cells retained; the harm is that the estimand and sample changed without the user being told, which is what puts it in case 3 rather than case 2. MIXED tail: for a contreat() user who meant contreatwithin — precisely the case the second caution line addresses — every period can lack a control, `ifvar' is zeroed everywhere, and the run then dies downstream at the L908 pre/post check or the L955 no-control-group check, i.e. case 1. A second MIXED note: the VAL-G10B comment above the block records that before the ordering fix this screen could delete a group's only reference row after that group passed the reference check, which sent a structurally broken sample "downstream to die opaquely at the dropped-dummy screen (r322) - or run silently wrong under safety(off) on some shapes" — but that describes the ORDER of the drops, which is now unconditional, not the safety-gated message.
evidence: The block body is only messages: "Caution: estimability checks found time periods exist in sample without a control unit, causing them to be dropped." and "If intending to only use within treated-cohorts variation in your continuous treatment variable, specify option contreatwithin to avoid these checks." The drop that causes it sits OUTSIDE the gate at L835: `qui replace `ifvar'  = 0 if `controlcheck2' == 0'. Header transparency comes from L11326: "N clusters = `Nclus'; N = `N' (`droppedobs' obs dropped from initial sample)".

checks: Under esfixedbaseperiod only: that the surviving treated rows straddle the reference period. One `gstats sum `_t' if `ifstatement' & `ttre' != .' feeding three asserts — r(N) != 0 (any treated rows at all), r(min) <= refperiod (a pre/reference observation), r(max) > refperiod (an observation past the reference period). Errors 459 with a message that adds targeted notes for timetrends and anticipation().
without_it: The run dies anyway, later and with a worse message. The middle assert is provably unreachable on its own: the reference-period screen at L856-859 has already zeroed `ifvar' for every unit that does not observe _t == esrelativeto, which the code states outright at L883-887 ("every treated unit reaching this line has a realized _t <= -1 and r(min) <= -1"). So the guard fires only when no treated rows survive at all, or when no treated row sits past the reference period — and both imply there is no treated observation with t >= ttre. `att' is the default estimand (L5163-5165), and the main margins call at L2030 is `qui margins [`weight'=`w_att'] , dydx(`targetflag') subpop(if `ifstatement' & `targetflag'==1 & `t' >= `ttre') ...' — an empty subpop. That margins is not wrapped in `cap', so Stata's own r(2000) "no observations" propagates out: a generic subcommand error that tells the user nothing about pre/post periods, timetrends or anticipation. If an event study was also requested (espre+espl > 0), the BS-33 screen at L1660-1700 usually intercepts first with wooldid's own error 459 ("no treated unit is observed at any of the requested event-study relative periods..."), which is informative but aimed at a different cause (onset-period gaps / off-grid onsets) and so can misdirect. I found no input that fails these asserts and still completes: an estimate cannot be formed from an empty subpop. The author's own cost review classifies this block as a cheap "core estimability check" and — unlike F13 — does NOT list it among the guards whose failure is silent.
evidence: Comment L907: "check that there is a real sample in that someone, somewhere, has a pre-period and a post period", and the message at L917: "Error: cannot find sufficient pre- and post-treatment periods for the treated units." The redundancy of the r(min) leg is stated in the file at L883-887: "the reference-period screen above zeroes ifvar for every unit that does not OBSERVE _t == esrelativeto, and esrelativeto is rejected above -1, so every treated unit reaching this line has a realized _t <= -1 and r(min) <= -1." review_process/guard_cost_2026-09-16.md screens it out as "core estimability check - the author's explicit carve-out. Also cheap: one gstats sum", placing it outside the silent-failure column it reserves for F13. The uncapped downstream call is L2030.

checks: Counts in-sample rows whose internal onset variable ttre is missing (never-treated units, plus units whose onset falls outside the sample window and so were set missing by oostreatedcontrols). If that count is zero — i.e. every in-sample unit is treated within the window — it errors r(459). Skipped under safety(off) and under contreatwithin, which does not expect a control group. Block runs 955-963.
without_it: TYPICAL TRIGGER (a staggered panel in which every unit eventually adopts, run on the default pooled reference): the run completes and produces correct estimates, so the guard prevents no failure at all — it is a design policy, not a correctness check. The mechanism is in wooldid_reltime at ado:12129-12155: 'gen controlcheck = _t == . & ifstatement; gegen controlcheck2 = max(controlcheck), by(t); replace ifvar = 0 if controlcheck2 == 0'. That drop is NOT safety-gated (only its caution is), so any calendar period in which every unit is already treated is removed BEFORE the regression. The remaining window therefore always has a pooled-reference (not-yet-treated) row in every retained period, so the cohort-by-period cell dummies are never collinear with the absorbed i.t fixed effects, and PS-63's measured 'N = 880 with 80 obs dropped' is exactly that terminal period being trimmed. This is what csdid (automatic notyet fallback), jwdid (notyet default) and hdidregress controlgroup(notyet) do by default. DEGENERATE TAIL (no treated cohort-period retains any comparison at all, e.g. a common onset): the trimming removes every treated period, _t comes back all missing, and the pooled path's own sibling guard fires — ado:12143-12150, 'cap assert max_t > 0 & max_t < .' then error 459 'cannot find either a treated time period for any treated units or sufficient untreated periods for treated units.' That is CASE 1 (an expressive early exit), and it is delivered by a different, better-aimed guard. ESFIXEDBASEPERIOD ARM: dead code. The fixed-base calendar-support screen at ado:828-843 zeroes ifvar in every period lacking a control unit, emptying the sample, and the pre/post sufficiency guard at ado:908-921 errors r(459) first, so line 955 is never reached. Only with safety(off) (which removes both) does PS-63's measured r(2001) 'insufficient observations' appear — CASE 1. Residual CASE 3 sliver, small: a shape where a cell dummy is dropped for collinearity despite the period screen; that is caught downstream by wooldid_ccscreen (ado:11818-11948) with 'Error: a treated cohort-period dummy coefficient was dropped for multicollinearity' + the offending cell, error 322 — again CASE 1, and only leaks where that screen's self-described 'imperfect' pattern match misses.
evidence: Guard text: "Error: you have no never-treated control group and no not-yet-treated control group whose treatment falls outside the sample window." / "To ignore this error, specify safety(off) or modify the sample window manually." Header comment: "given the above processing and estimability checks, do we still have a control group? note that the checks above should already trigger if you don't have a treatment group". Pooled period screen, ado:12129-12133: "produce a check that each _t interaction will be estimable in that there is an untreated cohort for it ... note that you can have periods with only treated units in them in the pre period provided they are periods pooled into an pooled reference period", with "Caution: estimability checks found time periods exist in sample without a control unit, causing them to be dropped." PS-63 (review_process/practice_sweep_2026-09-06.md:1785-1812): "with safety(off) the pooled default runs cleanly (att = .869, se .066, N = 880 with 80 obs dropped) and a full event study estimates (pre2 -.013, pre1 -.079, post0 .842, post1 1.057). Under esfixedbaseperiod the same data fails with 'insufficient observations', r(2001) - so the refusal is an identification fact in the fixed-base regime and a policy in the pooled one"; "the trimmed-window estimates are already computed correctly". Author's ruling (rulings_2026-09-07.md:80): "PS-63 | Leave as is. The refusal when every unit is eventually treated stands."

checks: SI-8 variable-count preflight. Three gegen tag() passes count distinct i levels, distinct treated (_i,_t) interaction cells, and distinct t levels, then forms si8demand = cells*(1+contreat) + ilev + tlev + 200. Two independent arms: (a) a caution if i has more than 100 distinct values; (b) a hard error 907 if si8demand exceeds c(maxvar). Gated on the USER's safetyinput (P6) and skipped inside replications. Block runs 1355-1378.
without_it: Arm (b), the only arm that guards against a failure: without it the run proceeds to 'reghdfe y ... i._i#i._t#i.targetflag ..., absorb(...)' at ado:1474 and Stata raises its own r(907) 'maxvar too small' partway through the expensive estimation, naming no wooldid concept and offering no remedy. The guard buys an earlier exit and a message that names the cell count and tells the user to coarsen i via fe(). The estimate is deliberately a LOWER bound, so the guard can only fire when the late r(907) was already certain — it cannot convert a would-be-successful run into a refusal, and it cannot make a wrong number right. Arm (a), the >100-levels caution, guards against NO failure at all: the run would return the identical, correct numbers, just slowly. It is runtime advice (cell count drives runtime at roughly its 1.3-1.7 power), not a correctness check, and it is the arm that fires most often in practice. Known leak, already open as a defect: the preflight did not fire on a 200x20 panel with i = unit (measured cells=2004 demand=2424 against maxvar 5000) which then died on Stata's own r(907) — the true requirement exceeded the estimate by more than 2x. So even as a CASE 1 guard the protection is partial.
evidence: Block comment: "The preflight uses the EXACT treated interaction-cell count (distinct (_i,_t) pairs, x2 under contreat for the dose slopes), a lower bound on the regression's variable demand, so an early refusal can only fire when the late r(907) was certain anyway." / "the preflight is the difference between an early named error and a late r(907) mid-estimation." Error text: "Error: this specification requires at least `si8demand' variables ... but maxvar is currently ..., so estimation would fail with r(907)." review_process/guard_cost_2026-09-16.md: "si8: resampling cannot create more distinct cohorts than the data has ... And the failure it pre-empts is r(907), which Stata raises loudly on its own." Same doc, incidental finding: "The si8 maxvar pre-emption did not fire on a case that then failed with Stata's own r(907) ... The true requirement exceeded the estimate by more than 2x" (opened in open_defects.md under OPEN).

case: mixed - not CASE 3 as defined: off-estimand cross-cell weighting when i-t cells straddle lattice bins, but the user is alerted by the ado:4831-4833 caution that prints under safety(off) too (this gate is a second lock, not the sole barrier); no failure at all when cells nest inside bins
checks: The cfx-plot production gate: 'if makecfxplots != "" & (item == "att" | safety == "off")'. The safety clause restricts production of the continuous-treatment lattice plots and the e(cfxatt_*)/e(cfxame_*) matrices to the att weighting; for att_it, att_i and att_itime they are withheld under default safety and produced only under safety(off). Block runs 2413-2638 (att and ame matrices plus the by-subgroup loop).
without_it: The relevant counterfactual is removing the item=="att" restriction (removing the whole block would just mean no cfx output at all, a missing feature rather than a failure). With the restriction gone, 'margins [pw=w_att_it] ... over(lattice_bin) subpop(...)' runs to completion for the cell-weighted estimands and returns finite, plausible numbers on a plot whose y-axis reads 'ATT_it on y'. Nothing is missing and nothing errors — the same code path already executes for non-att estimands whenever contreatwithin is specified, because that option rewrites safety to off. The numbers are nonetheless not the estimand the label claims. The mechanism is the weight construction at ado:1637-1646: w_att_it = w / (total w in the i-t cell), which sums to exactly 1 over a whole cell and so weights every treatment cell equally; margins over(bin) includes only the cell's rows that fall inside that bin, so a cell straddling a lattice boundary enters the bin with weight W(cell and bin)/W(cell) rather than 1. The bin's plotted point is then a share-weighted hybrid — neither the observation-weighted att nor the cell-equal att_it — and it varies with where the lattice cuts the cells. The author names exactly this containment condition for the same weights in the subgroup context at ado:1655 ("provided each i is always wholly contained in a given sg, we have no issues using these weights"). Secondary CASE 2 tail: a lattice bin holding no positively-weighted row returns missing, giving a visibly blank point rather than a wrong one. False-positive input worth noting: when cells are wholly nested inside bins (e.g. a unit-constant dose with a lattice built on it) the withheld plots would have been correct, which is CS-51's complaint that this is a fourth, undocumented policy class ("caution and withhold").
evidence: Caution printed at ado:4830-4839: "Caution: interpretation of continuous treatment effects plots for estimands other than the ATT is difficult unless i-t cells (and sometimes cohorts i) are wholly contained within lattice bins." / "As such, wooldid will not produce these plots unless you specify safety(off)." sthlp: "makecfxplots draws its continuous-treatment plots, and returns the e(cfxatt_*) and e(cfxame_*) matrices, for the att weighting only: for att_it, att_i and att_itime it prints a caution and produces neither the plots nor the matrices." consistency_sweep_2026-09-06.md (CS-51/CS-98): "Requested output is withheld unless safety(off) is given: makecfxplots with att_it/att_i/att_itime - under default safety the plots are simply not produced" and "the objection ... is about interpretation rather than computability". Weight code, ado:1644: "qui gen double `w_att_it' = `w' `customweighttext'/`w_per_it'" with ado:1624 "dividing w by w_per_it weights all i-t cells equally". guard_cost_2026-09-16.md classifies the site as "not a guard; output, and only under makecfxplots".

checks: Refuses `unconditionalse` when any cell-weighted estimand (att_i, att_it, att_itime) is requested, unless safety(off). Hard error 198 before any estimation runs.
without_it: Nothing crashes and nothing looks broken. Estimation proceeds through regress/poisson (the unconditionalse path, ado ~1457, ~1485) and every margins call gets `vce(unconditional)` appended to `marginsdof` (ado 1957). Point estimates are unaffected — the cell weights (w_att_i / w_att_it / w_att_itime, built at ado 1629-1646) enter as the margins weight exactly as they do on the default path. What changes is only the variance: margins builds the unconditional VCE from observation-level influence functions of a regression that was fit under a DIFFERENT weighting than the margins call uses, so the reported SEs, t stats, p-values and CIs are mis-sized — anti-conservatively, per the author's own simulation note. The user sees an ordinary-looking coefficient table with ordinary-looking SEs and unusually small p-values. That safety(off) is documented to 'proceed' is itself proof the combination runs to completion rather than dying. The only visible tell would be implausibly tiny SEs in an extreme case, which is a CASE 2 sliver, not the typical outcome.
evidence: Code comment + message: "*Issue warnings related to unconditional se reliability" / "Error: unconditional standard errors may be unreliable with non-att estimand types." The mechanism is spelled out in wooldid.sthlp:573-577: "When using aweights and estimands other than the ATT, tests using unconditional standard errors sometimes appear to be incorrectly sized, rejecting the null hypothesis at extraordinarily high rates. The issue with non-ATT estimands likely is related to the margins calculation doing computations on predicted values using different weights (weights modified to hit non-ATT estimands) than used in the initial regression... if safety(off) is not specified, wooldid will ... stop estimation if using them with a non-ATT estimand." sthlp:1207 classes it under "refuses, and safety(off) proceeds".

checks: Prints a caution (no error, no behaviour change) when `unconditionalse` is combined with aweights, unless safety(off).
without_it: Byte-identical output. This guard changes nothing at all about the run — it is pure text. Without it the user gets the same unconditional standard errors, computed the same way, with no indication that they may be mis-sized. The failure it prevents is entirely in the user's head: trusting a poorly-sized test statistic. Per the author's own note this does not always bite ("does not always occur"), so many triggering inputs are benign false alarms; but when it does bite the symptom is a plausible-looking table with wrong inference, which no competent user would catch by inspection. Note the asymmetry with 4617: the same underlying pathology (unconditional VCE is hypersensitive to weighting) is a refusal for the estimand case and only a caution here, because the author measured it as intermittent with aweights and observed that hdidregress shares it.
evidence: Message text: "Caution: unconditional standard errors may be unreliable with aweights." / "Set option safety(off) to suppress this caution." sthlp:573-577: "The issue with using aweights does not always occur, though when it proves to be an issue it tends to result in poorly sized test statistics for both wooldid and hdidregress... wooldid will warn against using unconditional standard errors with aweights... Broadly speaking, unconditional standard errors tend to be highly sensitive to one's choice of weights." sthlp:1210 lists it under "suppresses a caution, changing nothing else".

checks: Not a refusal — a message selector. Inside the `makecfxplots` + cell-weighted-estimand block (4830), it picks which text prints: under safety(off) only the interpretation caution; otherwise the same caution PLUS the notice that the plots will not be produced. The actual behavioural gate is elsewhere (ado 2413: `if "`makecfxplots'" != "" & ("`item'" == "att" | "`safety'" == "off")`).
without_it: Delete the whole if/else and the outer block at 4830 has an empty body — no message either way. Two different failures follow. (a) DEFAULT SAFETY, the typical path since safety(off) is opt-in: the gate at 2413 still withholds the plots and the e(cfxatt_*)/e(cfxame_*) matrices for att_it/att_i/att_itime, so the user asked for plots, got none, and is told nothing — a visibly incomplete result with no explanation (CASE 2; the run is otherwise correct, so the damage is a silently ignored option rather than wrong numbers). (b) SAFETY(OFF), which includes the internal relaxation `contreatwithin` + `contreat()` applied one line above at 4829: the plots ARE drawn, and without the caution the user has no warning that a cell-weighted effect plotted across lattice bins is not interpretable when i-t cells straddle bin boundaries (the same straddle the fastcollapse note at ado 5138 flags: "lattice() and makecfxplots split a cell on a binning of the dose, which is not part of the cell key"). Those plotted points look entirely reasonable and are wrong to read as dose-specific effects — CASE 3. I pick CASE 2 as the typical branch on frequency of default safety, but the CASE 3 branch is the one the author bothered to print in BOTH arms.
evidence: The two message strings, identical in both arms: "Caution: interpretation of continuous treatment effects plots for estimands other than the ATT is difficult unless i-t cells (and sometimes cohorts i) are wholly contained within lattice bins." with the else arm adding "As such, wooldid will not produce these plots unless you specify safety(off)." The CS-98 comment immediately above (4823-4827) confirms the block is message-only and that message/behaviour agreement is the whole point: "resolve the EFFECTIVE safety() value before any message keyed on it prints... doing it there let the caution below announce a refusal that the relaxation then overturned, so the run printed 'will not produce these plots' and produced them." sthlp:241: "for att_it, att_i and att_itime it prints a caution and produces neither the plots nor the matrices unless safety(off) is specified".

checks: Asserts that the cohort/unit identifier i consists of positive, non-zero integers over the estimation sample (`cap assert `i' > 0 & int(`i') == `i' `ifassert''), error 411 otherwise.
without_it: Three distinct branches. (1) i == 0 — the dangerous one, and the reason the message says "positive, non-zero". The internal cohort variable _i is built as `gen double _i = i if _t > 0 & _t < .` then `replace _i = 0 if _i == .` (ado 928-929 and the identical copy in wooldid_reltime at ~12177), i.e. 0 is the RESERVED sentinel for "reference period or never-treated". The treatment terms are the factor interaction `i._i#i._t#i.targetflag` (ado 1476/1485), whose base level on _i is 0, so a genuine treated cohort whose id is literally 0 has ALL of its treatment dummies swallowed as base-level cells: its treated-period observations silently join the control pool and it contributes no estimated effect. Nothing downstream catches this — the horizon-existence regex at ado 1671 ("anynumber not followed by a o or a b") is satisfied by the other cohorts, so relyrlist is non-empty and no error 459 fires; the F13 onset-constancy check passes (cohort 0 has one onset); and under att_i/att_itime the posttreatment coding at ado 1602 (`_i != 0`) additionally mis-bins that cohort's pre-period rows, corrupting its w_per_i denominator. The run completes and reports a plausible ATT that is a biased average over the surviving cohorts. CASE 3. (2) Negative or non-integer i on a TREATED unit: _i carries that value into `i._i#...`, which Stata's factor-variable machinery rejects (r(452), negative/noninteger values not allowed), so the run dies mid-estimation inside reghdfe/regress with a generic message after the sample has already been built. CASE 1. (3) Negative or non-integer values on never-treated units only: _i is 0 for them anyway and the reghdfe path absorbs the raw i as a grouping variable, so the run may well be entirely correct — the guard over-rejects here (the reg/unconditionalse path at ado 1485, which puts `i.`i'` in the regressor list, would still die r(452)). I pick CASE 3 as the headline because the zero case is the one the guard's wording singles out and the only one with no other symptom, though I cannot claim certainty about which violation users hit most often.
evidence: Message: "Error: `i' must consist of positive, non-zero integers, but does not" (error 411). The sentinel it protects is stated outright at ado 926-929: "* produce modified identifiers / * _i is unit identifiers that are positive integers if i is ever treated in sample and 0 otherwise / qui gen double `_i' = `i' if `_t' > 0 & `_t' < . & `ifstatement' / qui replace `_i' = 0 if `_i' == . & `ifstatement'". The base-level reading is confirmed by ado 1671-1673: "if regexm(\"`bvars'\",\"[0-9].`_i'#`horiz'.`_t'#1.`targetflag'\") { * the above regular expression resolves to 1 only if you see the following: * (anynumber not followed by a o or a b)._it#(horiz)._t#1.targetflag <- so a valid, included in the model estimate at the given horizon". sthlp:1207 classes it under "refuses, and safety(off) proceeds": "the cohort identifier not being a positive integer".

checks: For each of i, t and the as-given ttre: if the variable's storage type is float AND its in-sample maximum absolute value exceeds 16,777,216 (2^24), print a Caution. It is a caution only - nothing exits, nothing changes, the run proceeds on the rounded values.
without_it: Nothing crashes and nothing looks broken. Float cannot represent consecutive integers above 2^24, so an 8-digit calendar code or %tc datetime built the ordinary way (gen t = 20150000 + ...; float by default) was rounded upstream, pairwise-merging adjacent periods/cohorts/IDs before wooldid ever sees the data. Every other screen passes on the rounded values: i is integral and positive, t-ttre differences are still integers, ttre is still constant within i. The estimator then computes correctly on wrong inputs and prints a complete, ordinary-looking table. BS-34 measured the canonical repro (20 periods, 12 units, onset 20150008): rc 0, att = 1.3928571, se .0800771, t = 17.39, p = 4.4e-40, R2-within .5264, zero cautions; the double-stored twin gives att = 1.5 exactly. Note the guard does not prevent the wrong number - it converts a silent wrong answer into a flagged one (and the wrong answer is unrecoverable: recast double preserves the rounded values, only regeneration from source helps). MIXED tail, non-dangerous direction: coarse or even-valued codes above 2^24 are exactly representable, so the caution also fires on runs where nothing at all is wrong - a deliberate false-positive cost the author accepted because no exact detector exists.
evidence: Code comment 4967-4972: 'float storage cannot represent consecutive integers above 2^24 = 16,777,216, so an 8-digit calendar code, a %tc datetime or a large ID held in float was rounded BEFORE wooldid saw it: adjacent periods, cohorts or IDs merge with no other symptom and the run completes with a wrong answer. no exact detector exists ... so this is a caution on the only available signal - storage type plus magnitude (bug sweep BS-34)'. Message text: 'Its values were rounded before wooldid saw them, which can silently merge adjacent periods, cohorts or IDs.' review_process/bug_sweep_2026-09-06.md:1783ff: 'float gives rc 0, att = 1.3928571 ... and zero cautions - a clean, complete, wrong table.'

checks: Inside the contreatwithin + contreat() block, when contreatcontrols() contains byTime: under the user's own safety() (safetyuser, not the working copy contreatwithin rewrites to off), refuse the run with error 198. Under safety(off) the same condition prints only a Caution at 5172 and proceeds.
without_it: The run proceeds and estimates. contreatwithin declares there is NO strictly untreated comparison group - identification comes from within-treated-cohort dose variation - while byTime adds period-by-dose interaction terms (i.t # c.dose ringer, absorbed via contreatcontrolinserterABS, ado:1255-1256). With no untreated rows to identify the period dose slope, that slope can only be identified off treated rows, i.e. off genuine treatment effects. Two branches. (a) STAGGERED onsets (the typical case, and the one the author's wording describes): per fully-treated period the treated cell dose columns sum to the period column, so one cell is dropped per period and the rest are measured relative to it; the aggregate ATT/AME is an attenuated average taken over a zeroed cell. The table is full-rank, has ordinary SEs and p-values, and nothing marks it - CASE 3, plausible but wrong. (b) SINGLE onset / every period one treated cell: the period column spans the cell's dose column exactly, so the dose terms are dropped for collinearity and the ame rows come back as structural zeros with no standard errors - visibly broken, CASE 2 - and worse than the ordinary safety(off) presentation, because contreatwithin has already rewritten the working safety to off (ado:4829), which skips the collinearity family that would otherwise report them as missing with a naming caution. Typical input: branch (a), CASE 3. Confidence held to medium because I could not trace a measured example of either branch; the rank behaviour is inferred from the design of the control set, not observed.
evidence: Code comment 5168-5169 and its verbose line 5174: 'crash if probably illegitimate contreatcontrols are specified' / 'Typically, this partials out some treatment effects and yields unidentified estimates.' sthlp:1038: 'the control type byTime is refused in this case, since in the absence of an untreated group, the time period interactions will force wooldid to partial out genuine treatment effects for some group, threatening identification. Specify safety(off) before the run to proceed anyway, which downgrades the refusal to a caution.' sthlp:1209 on the internal relaxation: 'the ame rows print the regression's structural zeros instead of missing values, and without the caution that names them.'

checks: If the user supplied a weight expression (`exp'), assert it is >= 0 over the if() domain; error 411 otherwise. Gated on safetyinput (the user's own safety()), specifically so contreatwithin's internal safety-off rewrite cannot skip it.
without_it: No crash and no broken table. The worker's sample markout at ado:683 drops every row with w >= . or w <= 0 before weights are consumed by anything (qui replace `ifvar' = 0 if `i' >= . | `t' >= . | `y' >= . | `w' >= . | `w' <= 0), so a negative weight never reaches reghdfe, margins or the cell collapse. The run therefore completes on a silently narrowed sample and prints ordinary-looking estimates; the only signal is the dropped-observation count (e(N_dropped) and the displayed drop line), which is indistinguishable from the routine drops for missing outcomes or controls and never says the word 'weight'. So a sign error or a -9/-99 sentinel in a weight variable yields a correct estimate of the wrong sample with no mention of the cause - CASE 3 in the weak sense. COUNTER-EVIDENCE, worth recording: the author adjudicated exactly this and ruled the opposite way, holding that the counted drops make the outcome non-silent. Hence low-medium confidence. MIXED tail (inferred, not traced): if the whole weight variable is sign-flipped, every row is marked out and the run dies downstream on an empty sample with an unrelated message - CASE 1. There is no CASE 2 path.
evidence: Code comment 5238-5245: 'weight-sign screen ... gate on safetyinput, not safety: contreatwithin's internal safety-off overwrite sits upstream and previously skipped this screen entirely - contreatwithin + a negative weight ran rc 0 with no message (verifier s5_v2, 2026-07-26).' Worker markout ado:683: 'qui replace `ifvar' = 0 if ... | `w' >= . | `w' <= 0'. Author's rejection of VAL-G06 (wooldid_issue_file_rejections.md:55): 'negative weights can never enter estimation on any path (default safety errors r(411) at parse; under safety(off) the worker markout removes w<=0 rows before any onset/reference/support construction, and the drops are counted in the displayed N line and e(N_dropped)). No silent wrong result exists.'

checks: For a one-token lattice() that resolved to an existing numeric variable: assert every value is a non-negative integer or missing, over the if() domain; error 411 otherwise. Gated on safetyinput so contreatwithin's internal relaxation cannot disable it.
without_it: The run dies anyway, later and with Stata's own message. A passthrough lattice variable is consumed ONLY as factor-variable notation - local latticepart2hash ##i.`latticevar'' and latticepart1hash #i.`latticevar'' at ado:1089-1090 - which is spliced into the reghdfe/ppmlhdfe/regress call. Stata refuses negative or noninteger values in i. notation unconditionally (r(452)), and the reghdfe call at 1476 is qui but not cap, so the raw factor-variable error surfaces from the middle of a long generated regression command after all the sample construction, lattice and control machinery has run. The guard buys an earlier exit and a message that states the actual requirement. Missing values are deliberately tolerated by the assert because the markout removes those rows. There is no quiet path here: nothing multiplies or averages the lattice variable, it is only ever a factor. (Non-taxonomy caveat: the assert runs on the raw if() domain rather than the post-markout sample, so a negative value sitting only on rows that would have been dropped anyway produces a false error - the VAL-G06 domain complaint, which the author rejected.)
evidence: Code comment 5272-5275: 'one-token lattice() was previously unvalidated: a forgotten quantile count surfaced as a bare "variable all not found" r(111), and bad variable contents survived to the regression stage.' Message text at 5293: 'Error: the lattice() variable must contain only non-negative integers (it is used as a factor variable).' Usage site ado:1089-1090: 'local latticepart2hash ##i.`latticevar'' / local latticepart1hash #i.`latticevar''.

checks: When cfxlattice() is supplied together with makecfxplots and the user has not set safety(off): (a) asserts the cfxlattice() variable holds only non-negative integers on in-sample rows whose recorded onset ttre_asgiven is nonmissing (missing cfxlattice and never-treated rows are tolerated), erroring 411 otherwise; (b) counts rows where cfxlattice is missing but the onset is nonmissing and, if any, prints a Caution that margins will omit them from the continuous-treatment plot points.
without_it: Two asymmetric branches. ASSERT BRANCH (typical trigger: the raw continuous dose, or any non-integer/negative bin code, handed to cfxlattice()): nothing rejects it at parse time, the full regression runs, and the run dies later at the first `qui margins ... over(`cfxlatticeplot')` (line 2480) with Stata's own generic factor-variable/over() complaint about a non-integer or negative over() variable. The user has already paid for the estimation and gets a message that explains nothing about cfxlattice()'s contract. That is CASE 1. CAUTION BRANCH (cfxlattice missing on some treated rows, e.g. bins built by egen cut or computed on a subsample): margins silently drops those observations from each over() cell. Its own omitted-observations note is swallowed because every cfx margins call is issued under `qui`, so the run finishes rc 0, draws a normal-looking plot, and posts cfx matrices whose averages are taken over only the non-missing-cfxlattice subsample. Nothing in the output says so; the author records this as measured ('rc 0 with materially different cfx results'). That is CASE 3 and is the dangerous half. Note the asymmetry: the assert prevents a late crash, while the caution prevents nothing numerically - it converts a silent subsample average into an announced one.
evidence: Comment at 5299-5303: 'cfxlattice() content screens: margins over() accepts only non-negative integers, and previously bad contents died late at the margins/regression stage with generic messages. worse, margins silently DROPS missing-cfxlattice rows and wooldid calls margins quietly, so the omitted-observations note never reached the user (measured: rc 0 with materially different cfx results) - hence the missing-values Caution'. Message at 5322: 'Error: the cfxlattice() variable must contain only non-negative integers on observations with a nonmissing treatment onset (margins allows only non-negative integers in over()).' Caution at 5328: '...margins omits those observations when computing the continuous treatment effect plot points, so the plotted averages reflect only the nonmissing-cfxlattice subsample.' Downstream site, line 2480: 'qui margins [`weight'=`w_`item''] , ... noestimcheck over(`cfxlatticeplot') ...'

checks: Unless safety(off): asserts t - ttre_asgiven is integer-valued on in-sample rows (missing onsets exempt), i.e. that treatment onsets sit on the same grid as the time variable. Integer SPACING is not required - biennial or 5-year panels pass. Tiered: if the offending onsets all fall outside the usable estimation window (at or below the first usable period, computed as min(t)+anticipation, lifted to the second-smallest distinct t under timetrends, or above max(t)+oostreatedcontrols+anticipation), it downgrades to a Caution; otherwise error 459.
without_it: Fractional t - ttre flows into wooldid_reltime, which builds the relative-period variable as `_t' = t - ttre and then shifts it by min_t + 1 (lines 12081, 12165) before it enters the regression as i.`_t' factor interactions (lines 1462/1476/1485). TWO OUTCOMES, both recorded by the author. (i) Heterogeneous fractional parts - the common real-world shape, onsets recorded on a finer grid than t (month- or quarter-dated adoption against an annual t) - leave `_t' non-integer after the shift, so the run dies deep at the regression/margins stage with an opaque tempvar-named factor-variable error, a bare invalid-syntax, or a misleading insufficient-pre-periods r(459) that points the user at their panel length rather than at their onset coding: CASE 1. (ii) A uniform offset (every onset at year+0.5, exactly representable, so the min_t shift lands `_t' back on clean integers) runs to completion: the onset period is classified by the sign of t - ttre, so the true first treated period falls on the pre-treatment side and is absorbed into the reference window. The ATT and event-study coefficients come out fully plausible and are wrong - CASE 3, and the reason the guard exists. The tiering confirms the author's own reading of the stakes: onsets that would have been dropped or treated as never-treated downstream are harmless and get only a caution; the error tier fires exactly on onsets that actually enter the estimation window.
evidence: Comment at 5332-5339: 'non-commensurate ttre: fractional t - ttre previously either died late at the regression stage with opaque errors (a bare "invalid syntax", a tempvar-named factor-variable error, or a misleading insufficient-pre-periods r(459)) or - worse - ran to completion with the onset period silently mislabeled as pre-treatment. integer SPACING is not required - biennial or 5-year panels pass - only that onsets sit on the same grid as t. tiered like the F13 checks: offending onsets that fall wholly outside the usable window (dropped as pre-sample or treated as never-treated downstream) downgrade to a caution rather than an error'. Error message at 5361: 'Error: t minus ttre takes non-integer values, so relative-period horizons cannot be constructed...'

checks: That the raw user-supplied safety() token (safetyinput, captured before contreatwithin+contreat internally rewrites the working `safety' local to off) is either 'on' or 'off' when nonempty; errors 198 otherwise. Catches safety(OFF), safety(no), safety(0), safety(yes), safety(false) and every other spelling.
without_it: This is a typo-catcher, not a correctness guard, and the taxonomy fits it only loosely. A grep of the whole file shows every consumer of safety/safetyinput tests against the literal 'off' (`!= "off"` or `== "off"`); there is no `== "on"` test anywhere. So an unrecognized token is coerced to the CONSERVATIVE direction - it behaves exactly like the default safety on. A user who typed safety(OFF) or safety(no) meaning to disable screens gets them all enabled. Outcomes: (a) one of the screens they meant to bypass fires and the run aborts - but with wooldid's own specific message, often ending literally 'To ignore this error, specify safety(off)' (lines 957, 12266) - so it is an unwanted abort carrying a good message about the wrong subject, the user left wondering why their safety(off) was ignored; (b) the run completes with correct numbers plus extra cautions, and under makecfxplots with a non-att estimand the cfx plots are withheld (gate at 2413) with an explicit printed explanation. There is NO path to silently wrong numbers, because the coercion runs toward on: every safety-on branch either refuses, cautions, or computes more conservatively (e.g. wooldid_fcdeg at 5788 re-evaluates subgroups on the full data under safety on, and the safety on/off branches at 12086/12108 reach the same `_t' state and differ only in the caution printed). Case 1 is the nearest bucket - the guard buys a clear early message instead of a confusing late one - with the caveat that for many inputs nothing fails at all.
evidence: Comment at 5471-5472: 'tested on the raw user value (safetyinput): contreat+contreatwithin rewrites the working copy to off above, which would mask an invalid user token here'. Section header at 5450-5453: 'option-domain screens... each closes a silent-accept path: these inputs previously ran rc 0 with silently different semantics than requested.' Message at 5474: 'Error: safety() must be on or off.' Representative consumer form, line 955: 'if "`safety'" != "off"  & "`contreatwithin'" == "" {' with 5788, 4617, 12148 etc. all testing the same way; no `== "on"` test exists in the file.

checks: After wooldid_fcdegx has flagged the r() of a just-issued subgroup margins call as degenerate (an omission marker on a second-half name; a zero, missing, or below-1e-9-relative level variance; a contrast/pairwise VCE lying in a numerically singular direction), this block asks whether safety is on. If so it sets c_local fcrerun 1 and fcguard fallback, which makes the caller `restore, preserve` and re-issue that margins call - and every later subgroup call - on the full (uncollapsed) data. Under safety(off) control falls through to the caution path instead.
without_it: Removing the if-block leaves the fallthrough: fcrerun stays 0, fcguard becomes caution, and the caution text prints once (guard(caution) silences repeats on later calls). Estimation does not die; the subgroup results are simply read off the CELL-COLLAPSED margins call. The collapse changes the summation order, so in a numerically singular VCE direction an exact zero becomes a ~1e-16 nonzero or vice versa, which flips the branches wooldid takes on that zero: whether margins writes an omission marker (result suppressed vs reported), what rank -test- assigns the subgroup-equality chain (a joint test with different df and a different p), and whether a pairwise se comes back missing. Typical damage is a reported subgroup horizon or a joint/pairwise p that looks entirely ordinary but is cancellation residue and does not match the nofastcollapse answer -> case 3. The opposite landing (a pairwise se that comes back missing, a suppressed horizon) is visibly broken -> case 2, so the guard is mixed. Two honest caveats: (a) with the block gone the user still gets a caution, so it is not literally silent - the block converts a warned, summation-order-dependent report into a collapse-invariant one; (b) the predicate is broader than its failure - it also fires on structurally zero subgroup margins (e.g. an early cohort used as a subgroup, b=0 and V=0), where the full-data re-run reproduces the same answer and the guard costs only the speedup (which is why the `joint' arm exits early when margins returned no r(p)).
evidence: Header comment 5747-5758: "the subgroup section is the one place wooldid BRANCHES on a margins result being exactly zero: the omission marker margins writes into a returned name when b and V are both zero, the rank -test- assigns the subgroup-equality chain, a missing pairwise se. In a numerically singular direction of the VCE that zero is cancellation residue of order 1e-16, and the collapse - which changes the summation order - can land it on either side, silently changing which horizons and joint tests are reported (measured on 8 of 260 subgroup configs, every one in such a direction; none elsewhere)." Caution text at 5796: "an exact zero margins returns can be cancellation residue rather than an estimate, so which subgroup horizons and joint tests are reported can depend on the summation order - which the default cell collapse ... changes."

checks: Structurally this line is the UNCHECKED branch (safety(off), or esprelength==0 where the issue cannot arise): it blanks `_t' for horizons outside the requested pre-window AND for each unit's first observed period (t == mint) in one statement. The guard is the `else' at 12089: it blanks only the out-of-window horizons, then `cap assert `_t' == . if `t' == `mint'' to detect units whose first observed period is a period for which treatment effects were requested; when the assert fails it applies the identical replace and prints the forced-reference-period caution recommending esfixedbaseperiod.
without_it: No number changes. Both branches leave `_t' in exactly the same state (the else branch's conditional replace is the same `replace `_t' = . if `t' == `mint'', and outside `ifstatement' `_t' was never generated, so the missing if-restriction is immaterial). What is lost is purely the message. The run then completes normally and produces a full event-study table and plot in which some short-panel cohorts have silently had a requested pre-treatment horizon swallowed into their pooled reference period: the coefficients for those horizons mix treatment-effect contrasts with cross-cohort level differences. Nothing in the output flags it - the estimates have ordinary magnitudes and ordinary standard errors - and the help file states outright that the resulting paths can hide a pre-trend violation. That is the dangerous case even though the guard moves no number; it is a pure interpretation warning.
evidence: Caution text at 12095-12097: "reference period for some units forced (for want of panel length) to include time period for which treatment effects were requested. This does not break estimation, but event study estimates can carry counterintuitive meanings and reflect effect levels by cohort. Recommendation: use option esfixedbaseperiod..."; trailing comment at 12100: "If this condition triggers, event study coefficients are very difficult to interpret"; wooldid.sthlp:845-846: "cohorts with fewer observed pre-treatment periods will have their earliest observed period set as their reference period, even if this period is a period for which treatment effects are reported for other cohorts ... the resulting event study plots may show treatment effect time paths that evolve in counterintuitive and difficult to interpret ways, possibly obscuring even severe parallel trends assumption violations from detection."

checks: The timetrends twin of 12086. This line is again the unchecked branch: it blanks `_t' outside the requested pre-window and for each unit's first TWO observed periods (t <= mintp1, the two periods the cohort time trend consumes). The guard is the `else' at 12111: blank only the out-of-window horizons, `cap assert `_t' == . if `t' <= `mintp1'', and on failure apply the same replace plus the forced-reference caution (whose recommendation additionally offers dropping timetrends).
without_it: Identical data state either way - the else branch's conditional `replace `_t' = . if `t' <= `mintp1'' is exactly the clause the safety-off branch folds into its first replace - so removing the check costs only the caution. The run completes and reports an event study in which, for cohorts too short to spare two pre-periods for the trend anchor, a requested pre-treatment horizon has been absorbed into the reference block. The timetrends case is if anything more exposed than 12086 because two periods per unit are consumed rather than one, so it bites on longer panels too. Output looks like a normal event study; no missing values, no absurd magnitudes, nothing to prompt a second look.
evidence: Comment 12105-12107: "if using timetrends, never use the 2nd observation either - dont just always skip the first! the caution branch runs whenever a pre-treatment horizon is requested at all (bug sweep BS-2: <= 1 gated it off at esprelength(1), the smallest case it exists for)"; caution at 12117-12121: "This does not break estimation, but event study estimates can carry counterintuitive meanings and reflect effect levels by cohort ... (Or: request estimates for fewer pre-treatment horizons, or drop the request to include timetrends.)"

checks: Whether the estimability screen just applied actually dropped anything: `cap assert `controlcheck2' != 0' re-reads the flag computed at 12141 (by-t max of "this row has no requested treatment effect"), which is 0 for calendar periods in which every in-sample unit is treated. If any such period existed, it prints a caution that those periods were dropped, and - only when contreat() is in play - points at contreatwithin as the way to keep them.
without_it: Nothing about the sample changes: the drop itself happens unconditionally at 12142 (`qui replace `ifvar' = 0 if `controlcheck2' == 0'), before and outside this block, and `controlcheck2' is only re-read here. Only the message is lost. For the typical trigger - a staggered binary design whose late calendar periods have no untreated or not-yet-treated unit left - this is documented, intended sample formation: the retained estimates are correct for the retained sample, N in the header is smaller, and the help file states the restriction up front. So there is no output failure to classify; the taxonomy has no clean bucket for a guard that merely reports a documented restriction at runtime. The case-3 sliver is the contreat() user who meant to identify from within-treated dose variation: for them the dropped periods are the ones they cared about, the run still returns a full, plausible-looking set of continuous-treatment estimates from a silently different sample, and the second dis line exists precisely to steer them to contreatwithin. Extreme inputs (everything dropped) fall out later as the explicit error 459 at 12169-12174, not here.
evidence: Caution text at 12151-12152: "estimability checks found time periods exist in sample without a control unit, causing them to be dropped." / "If intending to only use within treated-cohorts variation in your continuous treatment variable, specify option contreatwithin to prevent these time periods from being dropped." Comment 12136: "do not apply test if not using a purely untreated control group (contreatwithin case)". wooldid.sthlp:194-196 documents the drop as ordinary sample formation: "the estimation sample wooldid uses may be more restricted than your overall sample ... and observations from time periods no untreated (including not yet treated) units are observed."

checks: F13 containment: that the subgroups() variable is constant WITHIN each i-by-t cell of the treated estimation sample (gegen min and max of the non-missing subgroup value by `i' `t', asserted equal over in-sample rows of units with a non-missing internal onset). Violation is a hard error 459 under default safety; under safety(off) the whole block is skipped.
without_it: The run completes and prints a full by-subgroup table. Nothing crashes and nothing is missing, because sg never enters the regression: the unit-by-period cell coefficients are shared by every subgroup a unit touches, and each subgroup read is just a differently weighted average of those same pooled cell effects. The by-subgroup estimates therefore differ from one another only through cell composition/weights, not through any within-cell heterogeneity, and the contrasts and their p-values look completely ordinary. A user with genuinely large within-cell subgroup differences reads off small, insignificant contrasts and concludes there is no heterogeneity. The one visible tell is the degenerate limit the comment names - contrasts coming back exactly identical - which a sharp user might catch; the typical non-proportional case yields plausible non-zero contrasts and no tell at all. This is the paradigm case-3 guard in the set.
evidence: Comment 12239-12243: "sg never enters the regression - the unit-by-period cell coefficients are shared by every subgroup a unit touches. sg varying WITHIN a unit-period cell therefore makes by-subgroup contrasts structurally unable to reflect within-cell heterogeneity (each subgroup only reweights the same pooled cell effects; contrasts can come back identical under strong true heterogeneity) -> error." Error text 12255: "subgroup estimates built from cells that mix subgroups cannot reflect within-cell subgroup differences - each subgroup only reweights the same pooled cell effects, and subgroup contrasts can come back identical even when true effects differ sharply by subgroup."

checks: The safety arm of the unit-splitting check. The detection itself (gegen min/max of the subgroup value by `i', asserted equal) runs unconditionally at 12267-12270; this block only decides the response: under default safety a unit whose subgroup value changes across periods is a hard error 459, while safety(off) falls to the else at 12277 and proceeds with share weighting plus a caution.
without_it: The counterfactual is "error becomes caution", not "check disappears" - strip the if and the dangling else's caution is what remains, so the user is still told. The run then completes with share weighting: by-subgroup att and att_it are unaffected (each observation is weighted to its own subgroup as usual), but att_i and att_itime enter a split unit into each subgroup weighted by its share of sample weight there instead of with the equal-unit weighting those estimands are defined by. The result is a table of ordinary-looking subgroup att_i/att_itime numbers computed under a weighting scheme that is not the documented estimand - plausible, publishable, and wrong by a margin the user cannot see from the output. The guard's real function is to force an explicit opt-in to that fallback rather than to detect anything new.
evidence: Comment 12262-12266: "a unit split across multiple subgroups over time (subgroup varies within i across periods) is refused under default safety - a unit cannot belong to more than one subgroup, and the share-weighted fallback deserves an explicit opt-in. under safety(off) the run proceeds with share weighting and a caution (author directive, 2026-07-28; this check runs regardless of the safety setting)". Error text 12274: "att_i and att_itime enter a split unit into each subgroup weighted by its share of sample weight there, rather than with the equal unit weighting those estimands normally imply." Mirrored in wooldid.sthlp:886-887.
